## What happens now
When I write a long description for a command, the command list in the help output shows nothing next to that command. The name is there, but the text that explains what the command does is empty. This happens when the first sentence of the description is longer than 45 characters.

## What should happen
Every command in the command list should always show a short version of its description. When the description is long, the short version should be cut at a word and end with three dots, so I can still tell what the command does.

## About this project
This project is a toolkit for building command line programs in Python. It helps people define commands, options, and arguments, and it produces the help screens that users see. It is used by many other tools to build their command line interfaces.

## Problem this solves
People who write long descriptions for their commands end up with a blank spot in the help list, so their users cannot tell what a command does. A short, always-present summary keeps the help screen useful even when the description is long.

## What changed
The help list now shows a shortened version of every command description instead of dropping it. Long text is cut at a word boundary and ends with three dots. ## Impact
Ease of use.

## User experience
Before: I give a command a long description, run the help, and the command list shows the command name with no text beside it. After: I run the help and the command list shows the command name with a trimmed description that ends in three dots.

## Plan for the ticket

**Files I read (both versions):**
- `/workspace/click/core.py` and `/megabit/.megabit_ref/click/core.py`
- `/workspace/click/utils.py` and `/megabit/.megabit_ref/click/utils.py`
- `/workspace/tests/test_commands.py` and `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_commands.py`

**What differs, in plain words:**

1. **The short description rule lives in two places.** Today the wrapping rule is written inline in the command setup code. The target version moves this rule into a shared helper in `utils.py` named `make_default_short_help`, and the command setup code simply calls it. The new helper also takes a maximum length value (45) as its setting.

2. **The current short-description behavior throws away long text.** In the current `core.py`, when a command has a description but no short description, the code takes the text up to the first period. If that piece is longer than 45 characters, it sets the short description to nothing at all, so the command appears in the command list with an empty description. If there is no period at all, the same thing happens — nothing is shown.

3. **The target behavior truncates instead of dropping.** In the reference `utils.py`, the new helper walks through the words of the description, stops at the first word containing a period, and builds up words until the next word would push the text over 45 characters. At that point it stops and adds an ellipsis marker. So a long description becomes a shortened line ending in the marker, and a description with a period inside the limit gets cut at the period with a period kept. In short: commands that currently show a blank description will instead show a clipped description.

4. **A test proves the difference.** The reference `tests/test_commands.py` adds a check that a command list shows two commands — one with a short text shown in full with its final period, and one with a long text shown clipped and ending in the marker. No such check exists in the current test file, and the current code cannot produce that output.

**Which workspace paths are about the problem (for the Hints section):**
- `/workspace/click/core.py` — where the short description is worked out today and where long text gets dropped.
- `/workspace/click/utils.py` — where helper functions for text live; this is where the new shortener belongs.
- `/workspace/tests/test_commands.py` — the existing command behavior checks, and where the current behavior can be observed.

**Ticket angle (problem this solves):** A person running a tool with several commands sees the command list with no description next to any command whose description is long. They cannot tell what the commands do without asking for each one's full help. The new behavior keeps a shortened line so the list stays useful.

**Notes for writing:** describe only the visible difference — blank descriptions versus a clipped description ending in a marker; keep the wording free of banned words and hedging, include no code, and keep Hints limited to the three workspace paths above.
